function: Joint design of transmit precoders and RIS phase shifts for max-min rate under reradiation mask constraints; the neural network outputs both directly (p. 9)
system: Downlink MIMO: transmitter 8 antennas, two 2-antenna receivers, reflecting RIS 12x12 with unit amplitude, no direct link, 27 GHz (p. 12, Table I)
method: Model-driven feedforward network (two hidden layers, 1024 and 512 neurons) with one-hot angle encoding, trained unsupervised with max-min rate loss, Adagrad, no labels (p. 10-11)
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rician fading (K=10^5) on transmitter-RIS and RIS-receiver links with free-space path loss; no dataset, loss computed from the model (p. 4, 12)
test_conditions: Angles within 10-60 degrees; tested on fixed angle setups, 64 antennas, three receivers, and 0.5 degree angle noise; no train/test split described (p. 11-14)
baselines: Classical: own alternating optimization (with and without mask), greedy search, method of [28]; learned: none, only a raw-input ablation of the network (p. 11, 13-14)
metrics: Received power versus angle of observation (beam pattern), minimum achievable rate versus number of RIS elements, running time (p. 11-14)
complexity: Big-O orders for AO and greedy search; measured running time: network 120.98 s, AO with mask 731.4 s, greedy UADP 859.27 s (p. 7-9, 12)
q1_support: p. 4: "We consider a Rician fading channel model"; custom simulator with path loss from [55], no 3GPP model, ray-tracing dataset, or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 14: "we consider a scenario where the input angles are affected by random noise"; this is only an input-noise robustness test, and no unseen scenario, dataset, or adaptation of a trained network is stated.
q3_support: p. 11: "For comparison, we consider four different schemes"; non-learned baselines are AO and [28] (p. 13), but no earlier learned method is compared, and the raw-input network (p. 14) is an ablation.
q4_support: p. 12: "the proposed model-based neural network achieves a reduced running time"; Table III on p. 12 gives 120.98 s for the network.
q5_support: p. 11: "training data and labels can be avoided by appropriately choosing the loss function derived from a reliable"; the channel is a custom simulator and no code or data link appears.
notes: Included: the model-driven network, trained unsupervised with the max-min rate as loss, outputs the RIS phase shifts and precoders, so a learned component performs area 3; the AO and greedy algorithms are classical. The 64-antenna and three-receiver cases (p. 13) change the output size of the network, so the paper does not show transfer. The runtime in Table III may include the training of the network.
